_comment: THE GAP CLASS REGISTRY — the machine-readable list `lens mint --class` validates against, staged by `setup` into <runDir>/records/class-registry.json. An absent or unreadable registry REFUSES every mint: a run that cannot name its own vocabulary produces a board nobody can interpret afterwards. Harnesses that build runs by hand — the fuzz, the seat probe, the tests, the golden scenarios — DECLARE a vocabulary through record.StageForRun rather than being exempt from the check.
_source: class-registry-seed.md — 224 gaps across three runs (retrospective 52 + efficiency 77 + sleeper 95), 38 classes, 97% of gaps landing in a >=2-instance class. That analysis is the PROSE; this file is the artifact the validator reads. Keep them in step: the seed explains why a class exists, this says which exist.
_extending: A class absent here is not forbidden — it is UNDECLARED. `lens class new` introduces one deliberately — with its definition, its nearest neighbour and the question that tells the two apart, on the record, and it binds for the rest of that run. That is the sanctioned path: the taxonomy grows by argument rather than by typo. A slug that earns its keep across runs is promoted into this file by a human, with its `material_default` — `always`, `never` or `by_grade`.

classes.definition: the living report's analytical core omits a structural element the protocol's report template requires (e.g. a graded likelihood x impact x complexity risk matrix), carrying the raw material only as unordered prose
classes.distinguisher: risk-cross-term-ungraded is two risks that ARE discussed but not jointly graded; structure-noncompliance is the ABSENCE of the required graded-matrix element entirely, for ALL risks, not just an interacting pair

classes.definition: a control credited with closing a gap cannot deliver that closure by its own operation — it fires after the decision it gates, acts on a variable that does not trigger the harm, erases the signal it was meant to distinguish, rests on an assumption the same document discredits, or is starved of its trigger by another control's short-circuit
classes.distinguisher: policy-without-mechanism is a policy asserted with NO enforcing artifact; self-defeating-mitigation is an enforcer that exists and runs and still cannot produce the credited closure. Against partial-control-coverage: that control works on part of the surface and misses the rest (coverage); this one fails on its own terms even where it does apply
